item.title: Lakebase: Managed Postgres for AI and Development
item.description:
Lakebase: Managed Postgres for AI and Development

Lakebase, a fully managed Postgres solution, enables developers to build applications with ease, as it allows any developer familiar with SQL or ORMs to start immediately. Storage is separated from compute, and the database resides alongside lakehouse data under Unity Catalog governance.

🔍 Overview

  • Lakebase is a fully managed Postgres solution.
  • It allows developers familiar with SQL or ORMs to build applications immediately.
  • Storage is separated from compute, and the database lives next to lakehouse data under Unity Catalog governance.

🧩 How it works

  • Every Lakebase project starts with a production branch.
  • Child branches can be created from the production branch for development, testing, or experiments.
  • Branches use copy-on-write, making a branch of a large database ready in seconds and only changes taking up new storage.

⚙️ Key details

  • Lakebase is used in various projects like Jevons Search, Branchflight, and BranchCut.
  • Jevons Search uses Lakebase branches to work on support tickets.
  • Branchflight provides preview environments for pull requests.
  • BranchCut brings Git-style branching and merging to creative work.

💡 Why it matters

  • Lakebase enables fast and efficient branching for development, testing, and experiments.
  • It provides a secure and scalable solution for managing data and applications.
  • Lakebase is used in various projects to improve efficiency and productivity.

#Lakebase #Postgres #AI #Development #Branching

Source: Branch, sync, serve: What our Lakebase Hackathon taught us about building on Lakebase

item.title: Microsoft Releases Semantic Kernel Starters for Multi-Language AI Development
item.description:
Microsoft Releases Semantic Kernel Starters for Multi-Language AI Development

📚 Introduction

Microsoft has released a new repository of starter projects for the Semantic Kernel, providing developers with ready-to-use code samples in multiple programming languages to accelerate AI application development.

📁 Repository Structure

The starter projects are organized to support different languages and runtimes. Each starter is a self-contained application that demonstrates fundamental Semantic Kernel patterns.

💻 Available Language Options

Starter Description
C# Hello World The Hello World C# console application starter for the Semantic Kernel
C# Console Chat A console application based chat starter for the Semantic Kernel
C# Azure Functions The Hello World C# Azure Functions starter for the Semantic Kernel
C# Azure ChatGPT Plugin The Joke ChatGPT Plugin starter using C# Azure Functions for the Semantic Kernel
Python Hello World The Hello World Python console application starter for the Semantic Kernel
Python Azure Functions The Hello World Python Azure Functions starter for the Semantic Kernel
TypeScript Console Chat A console application based chat starter for the Semantic Kernel
Java Hello World The Hello World Java console application starter for the Semantic Kernel
Python Azure Functions ChatGPT Plugin The Joke ChatGPT Plugin starter using Python Azure Functions for the Semantic Kernel
Python Flask ChatGPT Plugin The Joke ChatGPT Plugin starter using Python Flask for the Semantic Kernel

🚀 Getting Started

Developers can clone the repository using:

1

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel-starters

Then navigate to any sample folder and open it in their editor:

1

code <any-sample-folder>

Individual README files within each sample provide setup and execution instructions.

🔧 Development Options

The Visual Studio Code Semantic Kernel Tools extension allows developers to create new applications using the starters through an integrated workflow.

🤝 Contributing

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require agreement to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) available at https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com. A CLA bot automatically processes pull requests. The project follows Microsoft’s Open Source Code of Conduct.

™️ Trademark Information

Microsoft trademarks and logos used in this project must comply with Microsoft’s Trademark & Brand Guidelines. Third-party trademarks remain subject to their respective policies.

#SemanticKernel #AI #Development #OpenSource #Microsoft

item.title: Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2
item.description:
Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2

The Milvus Java SDK has been restructured starting with version 2.5.2. The SDK is now split into two separate packages: milvus-sdk-java and milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter. This change was made because BulkWriter requires a significant number of dependencies.

🧩 Available Packages

  • milvus-sdk-java: The core Milvus Java SDK package
  • milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter: A separate package for BulkWriter functionality

⚙️ Key Details

The Milvus Java SDK has the following requirements:

  • Java 8 or higher
  • Build tools: Apache Maven or Gradle
  • SLF4J is required for logging purposes and must be added to the classpath

Developers can add the Milvus SDK to their projects using either:

  • Apache Maven
  • Gradle

🚀 Availability

For Spring Boot applications (Java 17+), the milvus-sdk-java-spring-boot-starter package automatically configures a MilvusClientV2 from milvus.* properties.

Examples for the Java SDK are available in the examples folder.

💡 Contributing

Contributors should:

  • Read the contribution guidelines first
  • Refer to the DEVELOPMENT.md file for development information

item.title: Claude Code plugin introduces Karpathy-inspired coding guidelines
item.description:
Claude Code plugin introduces Karpathy-inspired coding guidelines

A new CLAUDE.md file has been developed to improve Claude Code behavior, based on observations of LLM coding pitfalls.

🔍 Overview

The guidelines are derived from observations on LLM coding pitfalls and are implemented as a single file to enhance Claude Code’s performance.

⚙️ Key details

The file outlines four principles to address common issues:

  • Explicit reasoning: Forces the LLM to avoid silently picking an interpretation and running with it.
  • Avoid overengineering:
    • No features beyond what was asked
    • No abstractions for single-use code
    • No error handling for impossible scenarios
    • Don’t refactor things that aren’t broken
  • Style and cleanup:
    • Match existing style, even if you’d do it differently
    • Remove imports/variables/functions that your changes made unused
    • Don’t remove pre-existing dead code unless asked
  • Traceability: Every changed line should trace directly to the user’s request.

The guidelines also emphasize strong success criteria to enable independent LLM loops, avoiding weak criteria like “make it work” that require constant clarification.

The “Goal-Driven Execution” principle transforms imperative instructions into declarative goals with verification loops.

🚀 Availability

The guidelines are available as a Claude Code plugin. To use them:

  • Add the marketplace within Claude Code
  • Install the plugin

This installs the guidelines as a plugin, making the skill available across all projects. The repository also includes a committed Cursor project rule (.cursor/rules/karpathy-guidelines.mdc) to apply the same guidelines in Cursor.

The guidelines are designed to be merged with project-specific instructions. They can be added to an existing CLAUDE.md or used to create a new one.

#ClaudeCode #LLM #coding #guidelines #AI #development

Source: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills
